task: Layer 4 council: what is a frame at travel time, what may a rebase change, and what must crossing a tier feel like?
protocol: council v1: one shared brief, two blind rounds (proposals, then cross-critique), no voting, chair triage
verdict: Recommendation recorded, decision pending (owner's D1-D5). Build A: address-origin frames, rebasing on tier crossings only, with the approach probe before the first line of the rebase module; the focus rebase is out of v1 and gated on that probe. The three seats all chose A and all put the same load on one weak point - a focus rebase that must either be stored (a second representation, and an under-specified shared link) or derived (deterministic but hysteresis-bearing). Removing it resolves all three objections at once and matches the evidence that every scene already normalises to its own scale. Dissent recorded verbatim: experience and shape want the focus rebase in v1; risk accepts either but insists it is derived, never stored.
notes: Two rounds, three seats, two model lineages. Round 1 blind and parallel; round 2 cross-critique with the other proposals pasted verbatim. No code written; every seat read-only. Notable corrections during the round: the experience seat initially claimed the perception rubric was not vendored - it is, at .opencode/skills/hillclimb/references/rubrics/perception.md, and the seat conceded and restated its 8/10 evidence in the rubric's shape. The shape seat changed its own signature so the frame layer keeps no content lookup (rebaseToFocus(camera, focus, address), caller resolves). The risk seat's crafted-cam claim was verified true: MAX_POSITION_M = 1e30 in src/state/url-state.ts, so a degenerate accepted cam currently renders a wrong image rather than reporting an issue. History rule tightened to: replaceState on rebase, pushState only on user-initiated arrival, same-addr pushes collapse, scripted oscillation leaves history length constant. Time rule tightened to: a mid-travel link pins the ARRIVAL t and the journey is derived from (addr, cam, t), never a stored parameter. The council cost is cents (three seats, two rounds, ~2.5k output words); no paid benchmark or visual probe was used.
